finalText:
The evidence is complete. Here is the diagnosis:

---

## Root Cause

**Readiness probe port mismatch on `deployment/c083-deploy`** — the probe targets port **9090**, but the application (busybox `httpd`) only listens on port **8080**.

The readiness probe has been failing continuously for ~2d17h (~81,000+ failures), so the pod never becomes Ready, the deployment has 0 available replicas, and the deployment is stuck in `ProgressDeadlineExceeded`.

### Concrete Evidence

| Observation | Detail |
|---|---|
| Container command | `mkdir -p /www && echo ok >/www/index.html && httpd -f -p 8080 -h /www` — listens on **8080** |
| Readiness probe | `http-get http://:9090/healthz` — probes **9090** |
| Pod event (81,316 occurrences over 2d17h) | `Readiness probe failed: Get "http://172.16.243.252:9090/healthz": dial tcp 172.16.243.252:9090: connect: connection refused` |
| Pod status | `Ready: False`, `0/1` containers ready |
| Deployment status | `0/1 available`, conditions: `Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable)`, `Progressing=False (ProgressDeadlineExceeded)` |
| No other resources | No Service, no other pods — the deployment is the sole broken resource |

### Additional Detail (path mismatch)

Even if the port were corrected, the probe checks path `/healthz` while the app only serves `echo ok` at `/index.html` (root `/`). The `httpd` won't return 200 on `/healthz`. So the fix needs to address both port **and** path.

### Impact Scope

- **1 pod** (`c083-deploy-7887ff6645-769zk`) perpetually NotReady
- **1 deployment** (`c083-deploy`) with 0 available replicas, `ProgressDeadlineExceeded`
- Any traffic routed to this deployment (via a Service, if one existed) would have no healthy backends

### Confidence: **High** — single clear misconfiguration, no other anomalies.

### Safe Remediation

Fix the `readinessProbe` in the deployment to match the actual application:

**Option A** — Point the probe at the correct port and path:
```yaml
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /          # app serves at / (index.html), not /healthz
    port: 8080       # httpd listens on 8080, not 9090
  initialDelaySeconds: 1
  periodSeconds: 3
  failureThreshold: 3
```

**Option B** — If a `/healthz` endpoint is genuinely needed, update the container command to serve a health endpoint and keep port 9090 with a separate health server.

Option A is the minimal fix. After patching, the pod will pass readiness, become Ready, and the deployment will transition to `Available=True`.

## Root Cause

**Readiness probe port mismatch on `deployment/c083-deploy`** — the probe targets port **9090**, but the application (busybox `httpd`) only listens on port **8080**.

The readiness probe has been failing continuously for ~2d17h (~81,000+ failures), so the pod never becomes Ready, the deployment has 0 available replicas, and the deployment is stuck in `ProgressDeadlineExceeded`.

### Concrete Evidence

| Observation | Detail |
|---|---|
| Container command | `mkdir -p /www && echo ok >/www/index.html && httpd -f -p 8080 -h /www` — listens on **8080** |
| Readiness probe | `http-get http://:9090/healthz` — probes **9090** |
| Pod event (81,316 occurrences over 2d17h) | `Readiness probe failed: Get "http://172.16.243.252:9090/healthz": dial tcp 172.16.243.252:9090: connect: connection refused` |
| Pod status | `Ready: False`, `0/1` containers ready |
| Deployment status | `0/1 available`, conditions: `Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable)`, `Progressing=False (ProgressDeadlineExceeded)` |
| No other resources | No Service, no other pods — the deployment is the sole broken resource |

### Additional Detail (path mismatch)

Even if the port were corrected, the probe checks path `/healthz` while the app only serves `echo ok` at `/index.html` (root `/`). The `httpd` won't return 200 on `/healthz`. So the fix needs to address both port **and** path.

### Impact Scope

- **1 pod** (`c083-deploy-7887ff6645-769zk`) perpetually NotReady
- **1 deployment** (`c083-deploy`) with 0 available replicas, `ProgressDeadlineExceeded`
- Any traffic routed to this deployment (via a Service, if one existed) would have no healthy backends

### Confidence: **High** — single clear misconfiguration, no other anomalies.

### Safe Remediation

Fix the `readinessProbe` in the deployment to match the actual application:

**Option A** — Point the probe at the correct port and path:
```yaml
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /          # app serves at / (index.html), not /healthz
    port: 8080       # httpd listens on 8080, not 9090
  initialDelaySeconds: 1
  periodSeconds: 3
  failureThreshold: 3
```

**Option B** — If a `/healthz` endpoint is genuinely needed, update the container command to serve a health endpoint and keep port 9090 with a separate health server.

Option A is the minimal fix. After patching, the pod will pass readiness, become Ready, and the deployment will transition to `Available=True`.
